llm.summary: FounderClaw is a large multi-agent toolset whose files and runtime instructions mostly match its purpose, but the install instructions, secret/OS access implications, and a detected prompt-injection pattern are inconsistent or higher-risk than the registry metadata indicates.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (multi-agent engineering team) matches the included skills and many code files (29 skills, browser daemon, CLI, Chrome extension). However the front-matter declares no required env vars/binaries while the repository and docs reference needing API keys (Anthropic/CLAUDE flow for LLM-evals), local Keychain/GNOME Keyring/DPAPI for cookie decryption, and filesystem access to ~/.claude/ and ~/.founderclaw — capabilities that should be declared. The remote install step (curl | bash) also expands the effective capability surface beyond what's stated.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells users (and the agent) to run network install commands (curl | bash from raw.githubusercontent.com, or git clone) and to modify agent config, create symlinks into ~/.agents/skills, and restart the gateway; it also documents actions that require OS secret access (Keychain/GNOME keyring) and copying browser cookie DBs. Those runtime instructions go beyond simple local-only skill behavior and include high-risk operations (downloading and executing arbitrary install scripts, modifying agent skill directories). A prompt-injection (system-prompt-override) pattern was detected inside SKILL.md content.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec in the registry, but SKILL.md explicitly suggests running curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/.../install.sh | bash and the repo contains an install.sh. Piping remote shell scripts to bash is high risk (remote code execution). The host is a well-known release host (raw.githubusercontent.com), but the action still fetches and executes remote code without first requiring the user to inspect it.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata declares no required environment variables, yet the docs/tests reference ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and other LLM-related usage; functionality (cookie import/decryption) requires OS keychain/credential access and the tool writes files to user directories (~/.founderclaw, ~/.founderclaw-dev, .claude/skills). The skill asks to modify agent config and may restart the gateway — these require filesystem and potentially privileged agent state changes that should have been declared.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true, but installation and contributor/dev modes explicitly symlink content into ~/.agents/skills, create persistent workspace dirs, and can restart the gateway. That gives it persistent presence and the ability to alter which skills are available to your agent; combined with remote-install behavior and secret access, this increases risk and requires explicit user review before granting.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing:

- Don’t pipe remote shell scripts to bash blindly. Instead: git clone the repo (or download install.sh), inspect install.sh and uninstall.sh, and only run them after manual code review.
- The package will create and modify files under your home dir (e.g., ~/.claude/, ~/.founderclaw/, ~/.agents/skills) and can symlink skills into your agent runtime and restart the gateway. Back up your agent configuration first.
- FounderClaw’s browse functionality imports and decrypts browser cookies and will prompt for Keychain / GNOME Keyring / DPAPI access. If you don’t want that, do not run the cookie-import/setup-browser-cookies steps.
- Tests and docs reference an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and other LLM tooling; don’t place API keys in a repository or .env unless you understand which components will call the external APIs. Prefer running E2E tests in an isolated environment and set EVAL env vars only in controlled runs.
- Prompt-injection signal found in SKILL.md: review any preamble or template code that might alter agent/system prompts or introduce persistent injected behavior.
- Safer installation approach: clone locally, audit install.sh (and scripts it downloads), run in a disposable VM/container, or run only parts you need (avoid running setup that symlinks into ~/.agents/skills). If you must install on your main system, read install.sh to see whether it downloads further code or adds remote cron/webhooks/telemetry endpoints.

If you want, I can:
- fetch and display the install.sh contents for quick review (do not run it),
- list the files that will be written/modified by the install scripts based on the packaged install.sh, or
- highlight occurrences of network calls, child process spawns, or prompt-manipulating strings in the repo for closer inspection.
llm.findings: [system-prompt-override] unexpected: A prompt-injection pattern was detected in SKILL.md content. FounderClaw is a multi-agent system that injects many opinionated preambles and templates into skills; the presence of 'system-prompt-override' patterns in runtime docs can be used to try to manipulate agent/system prompts and should be reviewed. This is not expected behavior for a skill installer and merits manual inspection.
